description:
# Fix B1: Provider dispatch — bare set_model routing (R1, R3, R15)

**Crate:** next-code-base (one cargo build). **Priority:** P0.

## R1 (P0) — OpenAI-compatible profile models misrouted to OpenRouter via bare set_model
**Verified code path (HEAD):** crates/next-code-base/src/provider/mod.rs:1825 (set_model), :1837-1841 (openai_compatible_model_prefix → profile-routed), :1847-1852 (named_provider_profile_model_prefix), :1904-1906 (forced_provider → set_model_on_provider(forced)), :1928-1936 (heuristic: provider_for_model → set_model_on_provider; else set_model_on_provider(self.active_provider())). selection.rs:17 — active_provider() returns **ActiveProvider::OpenRouter** for OpenAiCompatibleProfile/NamedProfile. src/cli/pager_agent.rs:3015-3032 (Face SetModel bridge).
**Symptom:** with an active OpenAI-compatible profile (e.g. opencode-go), picking a bare model via Face /model → :1935 set_model_on_provider(OpenRouter, model) → OpenRouter arm runs clear_active_openai_compatible_profile() (:1072) + needs_rebind → "OPENROUTER_API_KEY not found" or silent reroute to openrouter.ai.
**Root cause:** the bare-model fallthrough (:1935) uses active_provider() which is OpenRouter when a compat profile is active; the profile-aware routing (:1837) only handles profile-PREFIXED models.
**Fix (exact):** in set_model (mod.rs:1825), AFTER the forced_provider check (:1904) and BEFORE the provider_for_model heuristic (:1928), when `self.active_compatible_profile_id().is_some()` (or the active selection is OpenAiCompatibleProfile/NamedProfile) AND the model is not provider-prefixed AND not a known built-in → route via `set_model_on_openai_compatible_profile(profile, model)` (:1138-1184). Do NOT clear the active profile unless the model is explicitly openrouter-routed or a RouteSelection targets another provider.
**Regression tests:**
1. Active compat profile + `set_model("kimi-k2.5")` → openrouter slot NOT rebound; request targets the profile endpoint with the profile key.
2. Face e2e: default_provider=opencode-go, no OPENROUTER_API_KEY, SetModel{"kimi-k2.5"} succeeds; next request hits the zen/go endpoint.
**Real-world:** `next-code login --provider opencode-go` → Face → /model → pick any model → next prompt reaches opencode.ai/zen/go/v1 (not error, not openrouter.ai).

## R3 (P1) — Dotted Copilot model ids switch provider via global heuristic
**Verified code path:** provider/mod.rs:1825, :1908-1914 (normalize_copilot_model_name dots→hyphens), :1928 provider_for_model, :1932 set_model_on_provider(target). provider-core/src/models.rs:179,185,196 (provider_for_model resolves claude-*), :440 (normalize_copilot_model_name).
**Symptom:** active Copilot + `set_model("claude-sonnet-4.6")` → normalizes to claude-sonnet-4-6 → provider_for_model → "claude" → switches off Copilot.
**Fix (exact):** in set_model, when the active selection/forced provider is Copilot (session provider_key == "copilot"), route bare models to `set_model_on_provider(Copilot, ...)` BEFORE the heuristic (:1928). The forced_provider check (:1904) already covers the CLI-lock case; extend the same principle to the active-Copilot case.
**Regression tests:** (a) active Copilot + `set_model("claude-sonnet-4.6")` keeps Copilot runtime; (b) active Claude + same input normalizes to claude-sonnet-4-6 (preserve current).
**Real-world:** Face/CLI pick Copilot's claude-sonnet-4.6 → history shows Copilot, not Claude.

## R15 (P2) — MCP import_from_external() runs as side effect of every config read
**Code path:** crates/next-code-base/src/mcp/protocol.rs:522 (import_from_external in load_catalog_for_dir), :286-350, :339 (save_to_file).
**Fix:** move import_from_external out of the load path into an explicit migration step (setup/login) OR gate with a once-marker.
**Real-world:** fresh sandbox with .claude.json, `next-code doctor --only mcp` → no mcp.json created.

## Acceptance criteria (all must pass)
- [ ] R1 bare set_model routes to active compat profile, never clears/rebinds to OpenRouter.
- [ ] R1 real-world: opencode-go login → /model → zen/go endpoint.
- [ ] R3 active Copilot keeps Copilot on dotted model switch.
- [ ] R15 config read never writes mcp.json.

## Do NOT change
- The OpenRouter arm's needs_rebind logic for genuinely openrouter-routed models.
- The openai_compatible_model_prefix / named_provider_profile_model_prefix / explicit_model_provider_prefix routing (:1837-1898).
- The forced_provider lock (:1904).
- Existing AUTO_ALLOWED / DCG behavior.

## Build/test
`cargo test -p next-code-base` (+ provider-core if R3 helper moved). **Source:** docs/NEXTCODE-EXISTING-FEATURE-AUDIT.md R1/R3/R15.

title: Fix B2: History integrity — R2 cancel/abort poisoning, R9 Gemini thought_signature, R11 always-allow restore, R13 permission hang

# Fix B2: History integrity — R2 cancel/abort poisoning, R9 Gemini signature, R11 always-allow, R13 permission hang

**Crate:** next-code-app-core (one cargo build). **Priority:** P0.

## R2 (P0) — Cancel/abort poisons history (repair_missing_tool_outputs injects fabricated failures)
**Code path:** crates/next-code-app-core/src/agent.rs:1022-1103 (repair_missing_tool_outputs; inserts ToolResult with is_error:Some(true) at :1078-1093, persists :1103); turn_streaming_mpsc.rs:92-98 (call head), :1003-1017 (assistant ToolUse committed), :1427 (tool_handle.abort), :1470 (else-branch returns Ok), :1110-1121 (urgent-interrupt "[Skipped: user interrupted]"), :1458-1469 (reload path).
**Symptom:** user cancels mid-tool → next turn the model sees "[Tool output missing — tool execution did not complete]" as an ERROR and "repairs" phantom failures.
**Root cause:** orphan ToolUse (committed, no ToolResult) → repair_missing_tool_outputs fabricates an error result.
**Fix (exact):** In `repair_missing_tool_outputs` (agent.rs:1022-1098), when the orphan ToolUse belongs to an interrupted turn, mark the synthetic result as a NON-error interruption notice (`is_error: Some(false)`) — the existing TOOL_OUTPUT_MISSING_TEXT already reads "session interrupted before tool execution completed". Preferred: extend the existing "[Skipped: user interrupted]" pattern (urgent-interrupt :1110-1121, reload :1458-1469) to the generic abort else-branch (:1470) so a ToolResult is recorded for the in-flight tool before returning.
**Regression test:** unit-test repair_missing_tool_outputs with an orphan ToolUse + interrupted marker → asserts a non-error interruption notice, NOT "[Tool output missing]" error.
**Real-world:** start long tool, Esc mid-run, next message → model must NOT claim a tool failed.

## R9 (P1) — Gemini thought_signature dropped at tool-use persistence
**Code path:** turn_streaming_mpsc.rs:999-1000 (ContentBlock::ToolUse built with thought_signature:None); :543-552 (ToolUseSignature handled); turn_loops.rs:717 (blocking path forwards it).
**Fix:** `thought_signature: tc.thought_signature.clone()` at :999.
**Regression test:** assert ToolUse.thought_signature survives add_message_ext when populated.

## R11 (P1) — Always-allow lost on session restore
**Code path:** agent.rs:479 (init_session_allow_list only at create_agent); turn_execution.rs:1058 (restore_session_with_working_dir), :1084-1090 (clear_session_tool_policy); dcg_bridge.rs:1673.
**Fix:** call `crate::dcg_bridge::init_session_allow_list(&self.session.id)` inside restore_session_with_working_dir after clear_session_tool_policy.
**Regression test:** create agent+session, add tool to always_allow_tools, restore, assert classify_for_session(tool, sid) == Allow without prompting.

## R13 (P2) — await_permission_response can hang forever headless
**Code path:** dcg_bridge.rs:334-357 (blocks on channel only completed by signal_permission_response); TUI input.rs:2183-2213; server client_actions.rs:1162-1215.
**Fix:** add a timeout in await_permission_response (or auto-deny when no dialog handler registered) + surface a clear "permission required" error.
**Real-world:** `next-code run "edit this file"` headless → clear error, not a hang.

## Acceptance criteria (all must pass)
- [ ] R2 canceled tool → non-error interruption notice, no fabricated failure.
- [ ] R9 Gemini thought_signature survives persistence.
- [ ] R11 always-allow persists across resume.
- [ ] R13 headless permission → clear error, no hang.

## Do NOT change
- The normal tool-result path (completed tools always persist a result).
- The urgent-interrupt / reload "[Skipped]" handling (extend, don't replace).
- The DCG decision authority.

## Build/test
`cargo test -p next-code-app-core`. **Source:** docs/NEXTCODE-EXISTING-FEATURE-AUDIT.md R2/R9/R11/R13.

title: Fix B4+B6: Provider tool feedback — R4 Grok/Claude-CLI drop non-native tools silently
description:
# Fix R4: Grok/Claude-CLI (handles_tools_internally) drop non-native tools silently

**Crates:** next-code-provider-grok-runtime, next-code-provider-claude-cli-runtime, next-code-app-core. **Priority:** P1. **Depends on:** B2 (R2) — must land together (cancel still emits interruption notice).

## Root cause chain
- turn_streaming_mpsc.rs:1089-1103 `tool_calls.retain(|tc| NEXT_CODE_NATIVE_TOOLS.contains(..))`; NEXT_CODE_NATIVE_TOOLS = ["selfdev","communicate"] (agent.rs:63) while claude-cli advertises more (claude-cli-runtime/lib.rs:56,78-79).
- Grok ACP `ToolCall`/`ToolCallUpdate` → `StreamEvent::StatusDetail` only (grok-runtime/lib.rs:665-673), so no ToolResult is ever persisted → orphan ToolUse → R2 fabricates a failure.

## Exact ACP completion signal (Grok)
- ACP emits `SessionUpdate::ToolCall(call)` on start and `SessionUpdate::ToolCallUpdate(update)` on progress. The completion is signaled by a subsequent ToolCallUpdate with terminal status OR the end of the turn (session/prompt response). VERIFY which exact update the Grok CLI sends at completion (agent-client-protocol types in grok-runtime/Cargo.toml, features unstable_session_*).

## ToolResult mapping (target)
From an ACP ToolCall/ToolCallUpdate at completion, build `StreamEvent::ToolResult { tool_use_id, content, is_error }`:
- tool_use_id ← the ACP call id (the id that appears in tc.id of the next loop iteration).
- content ← the tool's final output text (from the completion update's result/fields).
- is_error ← Some(true) if the update reports a failure/error status, else None.
Producer: `GrokAcpClient::session_notification` (grok-runtime/lib.rs:654-678).

## Feed-back into the turn loop
- sdk_tool_results (turn_streaming_mpsc.rs:1198-1217) is keyed by tool_use_id; a StreamEvent::ToolResult flows in and is added as a user ToolResult block, then continue (no local execution). This is the intended path for handles_tools_internally providers.

## Retain-filter fix
Replace hardcoded NEXT_CODE_NATIVE_TOOLS retain (turn_streaming_mpsc.rs:1090) with the provider's advertised native set. Add `fn native_tool_names(&self) -> &[&str]` to Provider (default NEXT_CODE_NATIVE_TOOLS); Grok/Claude-CLI override with their full advertised sets. Do NOT drop a tool the provider advertises as native.

## Ordering / parallel / cancel
- Ordering: ToolResult blocks in the same order as their ToolUse ids appear in the assistant message (loop adds in tc order).
- Parallel: multiple ToolCalls → each completion produces its own ToolResult keyed by id.
- Cancel between ToolCall and ToolResult: must still produce a result for the in-flight id (R2 interruption notice) so no orphan remains.

## Expected persisted transcript (after fix)
```
assistant: ToolUse{id: call_1, name: "read", ...}
user:      ToolResult{tool_use_id: call_1, content: "<file content>", is_error: None}
```
No orphan ToolUse; no fabricated "[Tool output missing]".

## Test fixture (exact)
- crates/next-code-provider-grok-runtime/tests/fake_acp.rs: extend fake_acp.rs so session/prompt emits a ToolCall + completion ToolCallUpdate for a read tool; assert the provider emits StreamEvent::ToolResult{tool_use_id: call_1, content: "<file>", is_error: None}; and a subsequent complete() turn's transcript contains the ToolResult, no orphan.
- app-core unit: retain filter with a provider advertising ["selfdev","communicate","memory","session_search","bg"] does NOT drop memory/session_search/bg.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Grok emits ToolResult from ACP ToolCall completion.
- [ ] ToolResult feeds back via sdk_tool_results.
- [ ] Retain filter uses provider-advertised native set.
- [ ] No orphan ToolUse / no fabricated failure after a Grok tool call.
- [ ] Ordering preserved; parallel keyed by id; cancel emits interruption notice.

## Do NOT change
- NEXT_CODE_NATIVE_TOOLS default for providers that don't override.
- The normal local tool-execution path.

## Build/test
`cargo build -p next-code-provider-grok-runtime -p next-code-provider-claude-cli-runtime` + `cargo test -p next-code-app-core` + `cargo test -p next-code-provider-grok-runtime`. **Source:** docs/NEXTCODE-EXISTING-FEATURE-AUDIT.md R4.

title: Parity NX-PERM-002: Command-risk classifier + justification (P0)
description:
# Parity NX-PERM-002: Command-risk classifier + justification

**Priority:** P0. **Category:** UI/UX/DX/Logic. **Strategy:** PORT. **Best source:** jcode `crates/jcode-command-risk` (commit 659b8cc155) + CodeWhale command_safety.rs + hermes approval.py. **Blocks:** NX-PERM-001.

## Why
Every permission allow/deny today is opaque (allowed/denied, no reason). A command-risk classifier returning RiskLevel + Justification per command converts permission friction into trust and is the prerequisite for NX-PERM-001.

## Current nextcode behavior
crates/next-code-base/src/safety.rs:183 AUTO_ALLOWED (static allowlist) + bash-destructive gate. next-code-app-core/src/dcg_bridge.rs runs DCG classify. src/face_permission.rs surfaces the decision. None produce a RiskLevel or Justification.

## Reference (jcode)
crates/jcode-command-risk/src/{lib,gate,paths,tokenize}.rs: RiskLevel, RiskFinding, Justification. A tokenizer + path/arity analysis produces a risk finding with justification per shell command. The gate decides allow/prompt/deny and surfaces the justification.

## Target architecture
New `crates/next-code-command-risk/` crate (near-COPY from jcode, crate renamed). safety.rs/dcg_bridge.rs call it to enrich every BridgeDecision with a RiskFinding. face_permission.rs renders the justification.

## Data model
```rust
pub enum RiskLevel { Safe, Low, Medium, High, Critical }
pub struct RiskFinding { pub level: RiskLevel, pub justification: String }
```
BridgeDecision gains optional `finding: Option<RiskFinding>`.

## State / event flow
request_permission → classify_for_session → command-risk assess(cmd) → RiskFinding → decision → ServerEvent carries finding → Face renders it. Ephemeral (not persisted).

## UI / UX / DX
- UI: permission card shows command, RiskLevel badge (color-coded), justification line.
- UX: justification inline on card; Tab through; copyable.
- DX: `--permission-explain` (or NEXT_CODE_PERMISSION_EXPLAIN=1) prints the finding per decision; `next-code doctor` reports command-risk rule coverage.
- Keybinding: none new.

## Error messages
"Permission denied: <justification>". Auto-deny reasons must be human-readable.

## Edge cases
Empty command; sudo/su; pipelines with one dangerous element; shell metacharacters; Windows vs POSIX paths; unicode; long commands (truncate justification); untokenizable commands (conservative fallback).

## Compatibility
Do NOT change the allow/deny OUTCOME (DCG stays authoritative); only add the finding. AUTO_ALLOWED entries stay auto-allowed (RiskLevel Safe + "built-in allowlist").

## Files
- Create: crates/next-code-command-risk/ (Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/gate.rs, src/paths.rs, src/tokenize.rs + tests).
- Modify: crates/next-code-base/src/safety.rs, next-code-app-core/src/dcg_bridge.rs, src/face_permission.rs, Cargo.toml (workspace member + dep).

## Implementation steps
1. Port jcode-command-risk → crates/next-code-command-risk.
2. Wire safety.rs/dcg_bridge.rs to produce RiskFinding per decision.
3. Thread through BridgeDecision → ServerEvent → face_permission.rs.
4. Add --permission-explain.

## Test matrix
- Unit: tokenizer (arity/paths/patterns); RiskLevel mapping; justification text.
- Integration: known-dangerous command → finding attached; safe → Safe.
- CLI: --permission-explain prints findings.
- TUI: permission card renders badge + justification.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] jcode-command-risk port compiles as next-code-command-risk.
- [ ] Every allow/deny carries a RiskFinding.
- [ ] DCG allow/deny outcome byte-identical.
- [ ] --permission-explain prints.
- [ ] Card shows badge + justification.

## Do NOT change
DCG decision authority, AUTO_ALLOWED, bash-destructive gate outcome.

## Risks
Risk classifier false pos/neg. Mitigate: conservative fallback + human-readable justification.

## Build/test
`cargo build -p next-code-command-risk` · `cargo test -p next-code-command-risk` · `cargo test -p next-code-base` · `cargo test -p next-code-app-core`. **Spec:** docs/NEXTCODE-UI-UX-DX-FULL-PARITY-RESEARCH.md §10.1.

title: Parity NX-UX-004: Multi-tier compaction (proactive/semantic/preemptive) (P0)
description:
# Parity NX-UX-004: Multi-tier compaction (proactive / semantic / preemptive)

**Priority:** P0. **Category:** Logic/UX/DX. **Strategy:** PORT. **Best source:** jcode compaction-core + claude-code compact/. **Depends on:** B1 (provider dispatch) — compaction touches provider context.

## Why
Today nextcode compacts only reactively on context-limit error (with 5 retries). Long sessions degrade before the limit. Proactive (compact at threshold), semantic (embedding-pruned), preemptive tiers keep sessions productive — the biggest long-session pain.

## Current nextcode behavior
crates/next-code-app-core/src/agent/compaction.rs: note_compaction_applied:4, request_manual_compaction:34, try_auto_compact_after_context_limit:116, try_recover_after_payload_too_large:202, try_recover_oversized_openai_native_compaction:254, update_compaction_usage_from_stream:313, push_embedding_snapshot_if_semantic:337, fire_compaction_hook:356. Reactive only.

## Reference (jcode)
crates/jcode-compaction-core (commit 659b8cc155): mode enum Reactive/Proactive/Semantic + manager. claude-code src/services/compact/: 3-tier + micro-compact.

## Target architecture
compaction.rs gains `CompactionMode { Reactive, Proactive, Semantic }` + `CompactionPolicy { mode, proactive_ratio: f32 }` (default 0.85). pick_mode(context_usage, policy) dispatches. push_embedding_snapshot_if_semantic becomes Semantic tier input.

## Data model
```rust
pub enum CompactionMode { Reactive, Proactive, Semantic }
pub struct CompactionPolicy { pub mode: CompactionMode, pub proactive_ratio: f32 }
```

## State / event flow
update_compaction_usage_from_stream → if usage >= proactive_ratio × limit AND no recent proactive compact (cooldown cursor) → Proactive via request_manual_compaction. Context-limit error → Reactive (existing). Embedding snapshots → Semantic.

## UI / UX / DX
- UI: statusline/token-banner hint when proactive compact scheduled ("compacting at 85%").
- UX: no new keystrokes; sessions survive longer.

**Priority:** P1. **Category:** UI/UX/DX/Logic. **Strategy:** ADAPT. **Best source:** claude-code src/keybindings/{validate,schema,reservedShortcuts,loadUserBindings}.ts.

## Why
Users remap via keybindings.json; invalid keys / duplicates / collisions silently break. Validation converts silent breakage into a clear on-load error with fallback.

## Current behavior
crates/xai-grok-pager/src/actions/user_bindings.rs: KEYBINDINGS_FILE_NAME:36, apply_overrides:412, apply_user_keybindings:428. No schema/collision/duplicate validation.

## Reference (claude-code)
schema.ts (JSON schema), validate.ts (validate + reserved set), reservedShortcuts.ts (built-in set), loadUserBindings.ts (load + report errors).

## Target architecture
Add keybinding_validate.rs: (a) JSON schema check, (b) reserved-shortcut collision check, (c) duplicate-binding check. Returns Vec<String> diagnostics (already the return type). On error, don't apply the offending binding; keep defaults for it.

## Data model
```rust
pub struct KeybindingValidation { pub errors: Vec<String>, pub applied: Vec<ParsedOverride> }
```
Reserved set is &[&str] of built-in default shortcuts.

## State / event flow
Startup/reload → apply_user_keybindings → validate → diagnostics → toast + partial apply (or full fallback).

## UI / UX / DX
- UI: load toast lists each error (e.g. "ctrl+k collides with which-key"); which-key shows effective bindings.
- UX: no new keystrokes; effective binding never silently wrong.
- DX: keybindings.json schema in docs; next-code doctor validates; NEXT_CODE_STRICT_KEYBINDINGS=1 promotes warnings to errors.
- Keybinding: validation applies to user file only; built-ins authoritative; user binding equal to reserved built-in rejected by default; "override_reserved":true opt-in.

## Error messages
"keybindings.json: line N: invalid key \"foo\"" · "collision: ctrl+k reserved for which-key" · "duplicate: ctrl+r bound twice".

## Edge cases
Malformed JSON; empty file; unknown action id; modifier combos; case sensitivity; Windows ctrl vs mac cmd; trailing whitespace.

# Parity NX-UX-001: Streaming markdown-table holdback (live reflow)

**Priority:** P1. **Category:** UI/UX/Logic. **Strategy:** ADAPT. **Best source:** codex streaming/table_holdback.rs. **Build cost:** HIGH (scrollback streaming).

## Why
Streaming markdown tables commit as raw text → columns misalign, table jumps. Holdback keeps in-progress tables as a live mutable tail that reflows until close.

## Current behavior

## Reference (codex)
.tmp/codex/streaming/table_holdback.rs — buffers a streaming markdown table into a live reflowable block; rows realign until closing delimiter or non-table line.

## Target architecture
In the streaming block renderer, detect a table tail; buffer it; reflow column widths as rows stream; commit when the table closes or a non-table line arrives.

## Data model
```rust
pub struct TableTail { pub rows: Vec<Vec<String>>, pub col_widths: Vec<usize>, pub in_table: bool }
```

## State / event flow
TextDelta → block buffer → if tail is table → TableTail reflow → render; else commit as before.

## UI / UX / DX
- UI: in-progress table renders aligned, reflows as rows arrive; optional "table streaming" indicator.
- UX: no new keystrokes; tables render cleanly while streaming.
- DX: config streaming_table_holdback (default true).

## Edge cases
Table never closes (timeout → commit); escaped pipes; multi-line cells; tables interleaved with code; a | line that isn't a table.

## Compatibility
Non-table streaming byte-identical. Only detected table rows affected.

## Files
- Modify: crates/xai-grok-pager/src/scrollback/ (block streaming + render).
- Create: crates/xai-grok-pager/src/scrollback/table_tail.rs.

## Implementation steps
1. Port table-tail detection + reflow from codex into table_tail.rs.
2. Hook into the streaming block renderer.
3. Add config + commit-on-close/timeout.

## Test matrix
- Unit: detect table; reflow widths; close commits; non-table line commits.
- Snapshot: streaming table aligned.
- Real-world: model emits a table → aligned non-jumping render.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] In-progress tables reflow aligned.
- [ ] Close commits the table.
- [ ] Non-table lines unaffected.
- [ ] Config toggle works.

Non-table text streaming and the existing block commit logic.

# Parity NX-UX-003: Parallel tool scheduler (concurrency-bounded batching)

**Priority:** P1. **Category:** Logic/UX. **Strategy:** REIMPLEMENT. **Best source:** gemini-cli core/src/scheduler/scheduler.ts:472-576. **Depends on:** B2 (history integrity — scheduler touches the tool loop).

## Why
Parallel tool calls execute serially today. A concurrency-bounded scheduler cuts latency for batches of independent tools.

## Current behavior
crates/next-code-app-core/src/agent/turn_loops.rs executes provider tool calls in a loop; no explicit concurrency-bound scheduler. turn_streaming_mpsc.rs:1108 per-tool loop.

## Reference (gemini-cli)
scheduler.ts:472-576 — explicit batching of contiguous parallelizable tools with a concurrency bound; dependent tools wait; results aggregate in order.

## Target architecture
A scheduler that groups contiguous independent tool calls, runs them concurrently up to a configurable bound, preserves result ordering.

## Data model
```rust
pub struct ToolScheduler { pub concurrency: usize, pub groups: Vec<Vec<ToolCall>> }
```

## State / event flow
tool_calls → scheduler partitions into groups → dispatch concurrently → collect results in order → feed ToolResult messages.

## UI / UX / DX
- UI: concurrent tools render as parallel progress (existing tool cards) + "running N tools" indicator.
- UX: no new keystrokes; parallel batches faster.
- DX: config tool_concurrency (default 4; 1 = serial, current behavior).

## Edge cases
Side-effecting tools that must be serial (bash writes); partial failure in a batch; cancel mid-batch; dependent-call ordering; provider parallel-call limits.

## Compatibility
tool_concurrency=1 byte-identical to today. Default conservative (parallel only for clearly-independent calls).

## Files
- Modify: crates/next-code-app-core/src/agent/turn_loops.rs, config types.
- Create: crates/next-code-app-core/src/agent/tool_scheduler.rs.

## Implementation steps
1. Port scheduler into tool_scheduler.rs.
2. Wire into tool-exec loop.
3. Add config; default conservative.

## Test matrix
- Unit: group independent vs dependent; concurrency bound; result ordering.
- State: partial batch failure handled.
- Real-world: 3 independent read calls run concurrently, results in order.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Independent tools batch + run concurrently.
- [ ] Result order preserved.
- [ ] Dependent calls serialized.
- [ ] tool_concurrency honored; 1 = serial.

## Do NOT change
Serial path at concurrency=1; tool-result message ordering.

## Risks
Parallel side-effecting tools racing. Mitigate: only batch provider-marked-parallelizable; conservative default.

## Build/test

## Target architecture
A startup gate: if cwd has no recorded trust state, show a dialog (Face) / prompt (CLI) before connect/config; persist decision keyed by folder path.

## Data model
```rust
pub struct FolderTrust { pub path: PathBuf, pub trusted: bool, pub always: bool }
```
Persisted in ~/.next-code/trust.json.

## State / event flow
Startup → resolve cwd trust → untrusted → dialog → decision → persist → proceed.

## UI / UX / DX
- UI: Face modal "Trust this folder? [Trust] [Don't trust] [Always trust this folder]".
- UX: arrow keys select; Enter confirms; choice persists.
- DX: CLI next-code run prompts on stdin; --trust / --no-trust skip; config folder_trust.

## Compatibility

# Fix R10: CLI --model vs config default_model precedence

**Crate:** src/cli (commands.rs, provider_init.rs) + next-code-app-core. **Priority:** P2. **Depends on:** B1.

run_single_message_command applies --model via init_provider_quiet (src/cli/provider_init.rs:1824-1831), then Agent::new (src/cli/commands.rs:2271-2276) runs apply_config_default_model (crates/next-code-app-core/src/agent.rs:293-325, called at :458) which unconditionally re-applies config default_model, clobbering the flag.

Gate apply_config_default_model on "no explicit model was resolved": thread an "explicit model" flag from init_provider_quiet/Agent::new, OR set the model again after Agent::new in run_single_message_command.

## Real-world

# Fix Provider hardening — R12 OpenRouter SSE retry, R14 OpenAI 429, R18 Anthropic deltas, R19 401/403

**Crates:** provider-openrouter-runtime, provider-openai-runtime, provider-anthropic-runtime, provider-core. **Priority:** P2.

## R12 (P2) — OpenRouter mid-stream SSE error bypasses retry classifier
crates/next-code-provider-openrouter-runtime/src/openrouter_sse_stream.rs:247-276 forwards StreamEvent::Error with no is_retryable_error check (OpenAI bails, Anthropic bails). Fix: before tx.send, if Error matches is_retryable_error → return Err (mirror OpenAI/Anthropic). Regression: feed `data: {"error":{"message":"Overloaded","code":529}}` → stream_response returns Err.

## R14 (P2) — OpenAI 429 retry depends on literal "rate limit" phrase
openai_stream_runtime.rs:223-227,1542-1544. Fix: short-circuit on actual status (prefix 429 message with canonical "429 too many requests" or thread StatusCode into is_retryable_error); fix the test asserting a string that never occurs (:1619-1625).

## R18 (P2) — Anthropic redacted_thinking_delta / unknown deltas silently dropped
anthropic-runtime/lib.rs:2204-2224,2356-2370. Fix: catch-all/[serde(other)] variant that logs unknown delta types; emit ThinkingDelta("") for redacted so thinking lifecycle stays coherent.

## R19 (P2) — Embedded 401/403 text in error body classified as retryable
provider-core failover.rs:435-499 runs contains_independent_status_code on embedded "401"/"403" even when status_code is None. Fix: gate embedded-code matching on a real HTTP status context.

## Acceptance criteria (per fix)
- [ ] R12 mid-stream 429/5xx retries, not silent end.
- [ ] R14 429 with generic body retried per Retry-After.
- [ ] R18 redacted delta renders coherent empty reasoning, logged.
- [ ] R19 deterministic auth errors not retried.

## Do NOT change
The retry classifier's existing happy paths; provider success paths.
